newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ school leaving age to stay at 16 - Creech.
newsitem.headline: NZ school leaving age to stay at 16 - Creech.

text.p: The New Zealand school leaving age will remain at 16 years next year, education minister Wyatt Creech said on Tuesday.

The National government announced in 1995 it planned to lift the school leaving age to 17 years from January 1, 1998, to coincide with the full implementation of the National Qualifications Framework.
Creech said the government would instead put more energy and resources into improving the responsiveness of schools so that students benefited from staying at school longer.
Creech said the National Qualifications policy was still under development and it would be premature to raise the school leaving age to 17 at this stage.
